title: Ops Coda: Release Annotated Slate and Sounding Board
body:
Purpose:
This doc is a compact operational coda for the Nov 2026 rollout window. It's intended to be used during the 72h preflight, the staggered regional rollout, and the 48h stabilization window. Use as a quick reference (crew pocket manual) and as the customer-facing release notes draft for the initial opt-in wave.

Summary of the release:
- Scope: Serving runtime v2.8.1 (kv-cache prefault, small attention kernel update, improved quantized matmul path).
- Primary goal: Reduce 95th p99 latency by ~8–12% on short sequences (<256) while preserving throughput for batching-heavy load.
- Risk surface: kernel path changes affecting older CUDA drivers (narrow), edge-case kv-prefetch race seen on very-high-concurrency tests (mitigation included).
- Expected user-visible change: Slight latency improvement; no API changes.

Key dates (compact calendar):
- 2026-11-08: Internal dry-run in staging (smoke + load). Owners: Marcus (runtime), Lena (infra).
- 2026-11-09: Canary prep and canary-only traffic split config checked-in. Owner: Priya.
- 2026-11-10 02:00–08:00 UTC: Canary wave 1 (US-EAST) — 2% traffic.
- 2026-11-10 08:00–14:00 UTC: Canary wave 2 (US-EAST) — 10% traffic.
- 2026-11-10 18:00–23:59 UTC: Canary wave 3 (US-WEST) — 10% traffic.
- 2026-11-11: Regional ramp (EU) — 25% -> 50% over 6h with telemetry checks.
- 2026-11-12: Global ramp to 100% with safety lanes and rollback window.
- 2026-11-14 to 2026-11-15: Post-release validation and early-retro.

Rollout cadence and ramp rules (explicit):
- Canary -> staged regional ramps -> global.
- Minimum observation window between ramps: 90 minutes unless explicit sign-off.
- If any of the primary signals degrade beyond thresholds (see "Signals & thresholds"), automatically pause ramp and escalate.
- Fallback policy: roll back to v2.8.0 on affected subpool. Full rollback requires Ops Conductor approval (on-call + release lead).

Canary percentages by lane:
- Wave 1: 2% (US-EAST AZ1)
- Wave 2: 10% (US-EAST AZ1+AZ2)
- Wave 3: 10% (US-WEST single AZ)
- Wave 4: 25% (EU single region)
- Wave 5: 50% (EU + NA secondary regions)

Signals & thresholds (what to watch):
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 token and request latency. Alert if p95 > baseline + 15% or p99 > baseline + 25%.
- Error rate: 5xx increase > 0.5 percentage points over baseline (rolling 10m) -> pause.
- Token-drop anomalies: any client-observed incomplete streams > 0.1% of requests -> immediate investigation.
- Resource saturation: GPU memory OOMs, host CPU > 85% sustained -> stop ramp and pin to previous revision.
- Cost spike heuristic: per-token cost jump > 20% without latency improvements -> throttling decision.

Smoke test matrix (quick checks to run during each wave):
- Basic generation (short prompt) -> verify completion and correct tokenization.
- Long-context handling (>=1024 tokens) -> verify KV cache integrity and no corruption.
- Streaming stability -> open/close reconnects, partial retransmits.
- Embeddings endpoint -> sample similarity checks vs baseline.
- Load-stepped throughput -> ramp 1k -> 5k -> 10k req/min and observe tail latencies.
- Canary-specific: run the kv-prefetch regression harness (20m) to look for rare race failures.

Ownership & escalation (quick roster):
- Release lead: Ethan Morales (primary contact).
- Runtime SME: Marcus Chen (executes hotfixes if needed).
- Infra/Autoscale: Lena Ortiz (manages pool sizing, burst config).
- Observability/Telemetry: Priya Gupta (dashboards and signal triage).
- Customer comms / CS sync: Aisha Rahman (prepares customer notes and handles early outreach).
- On-call rotation during rollout: see attached on-call mini-roster (link above).

Rollback decision matrix (condensed):
- Immediate rollback triggers (no debate): GPU OOMs across >2 hosts in a pool, systemic data corruption, catastrophic security bug.
- Pause & triage triggers: sustained p99 violations > 30% over baseline for 30 minutes, error rate up by >1% sustained.
- Partial rollback: if issue isolated to a region or AZ, roll back that subpool and continue elsewhere.

Customer-facing release notes (draft — concise):
Title: Faster short-sequence responses across Redwood’s hosted inference (v2.8.1)
Body draft:
We’re rolling out a performance improvement to our inference runtime that reduces latency for many short-sequence generation requests. This update is focused on backend optimizations and does not change model APIs or request/response formats.
What to expect:
- Slightly lower response latency for short prompts (<256 tokens) in most regions.
- No changes to billing or usage metrics.
- If you see unexpected errors, contact support@redwood.ai or use the in-console support button — include request IDs and timestamps.
Notes for platform owners: we recommend verifying client-side retry windows are at least 10s to avoid interfering with streaming reconnects during rollout.

Internal comms plan (short):
- Preflight 24h: Slack alert to #release-orchestra with checklist.
- Start: pinned message with live runbook snippet and link to timeline.
- During: round-robin updates every ramp step (Ops Conductor posts summary).
- Post: retrospective invite and brief in #eng-release with link to postmortem doc.

Unknowns / open questions (soundboard):
- Should API clients receive a proactive advisory for any users that pin to older CUDA drivers? (Priya to advise)
- Consider an additional lightweight AB measurement for quality regression on a small set of high-value customers — cost vs benefit? (Aisha)
- Decision: allow burst-capacity scaling during wave 3 in US-WEST? Deferred to Lena + release lead.

Preflight checklist (tick box style, used during T-72h -> T-0):
- [ ] Merge release PR and sign off CI (Ethan).
- [ ] Staging dry-run passed (Marcus, Lena).
- [ ] Canary split config validated in infra repo (Priya).
- [ ] Dashboards and alerting thresholds deployed (Priya).
- [ ] Customer comms draft approved (Aisha).
- [ ] Rollback artifact accessible and tested (binary pin + infra rollback policy) (Lena).
- [ ] On-call schedule published and NR invite sent (Ethan).
- [ ] Runbooks and smoke harness accessible in staging (Marcus).

Post-release checklist (T+0 -> T+72h):
- [ ] Verify global telemetry aggregated and compare to baseline (Priya).
- [ ] Customer issues triaged within 2h SLA (Aisha + CS).
- [ ] Hotfix cadence defined if required (Marcus).
- [ ] Early retrospective notes captured, assign action items (Ethan).

Notes to reviewers (ask list):
- Please scan the Signals & thresholds section for missing telemetry that you rely on.
- If you own any model-onboarding flows that call into runtime, confirm there are no hidden assumptions about kernel behavior.
- Comment inline for any language you want adjusted in the customer-facing note.

Appendix (quick links & artifacts):
- Load test harness: link in linked_artifacts above.
- Regression script: GITHUB PR 1427 contains the kv-prefetch test harness.
- Staging snapshot: confluence page in linked_artifacts.

Quick retrospective prompts (for postmortem):
- What went well?
- What tripped us up and why?
- Any telemetry gaps that delayed detection?
- How repeatable is the rollback for partial-region issues?
- Owners for follow-ups (assign within 48h).

---
Informal notes to self (Ethan):
- Keep wave windows conservative — ops fatigue from late-night ramps is real.
- If we see odd streaming reconnect patterns, suspect the new kernel backpressure heuristics first.
- Prioritize customer-facing clarity: small perf wins — avoid heavy technical details in initial note.

End of slate.
